      The rates above are based on the Member maintaining at all times a power factor of 90%
     (lagging) or higher as determined by measurement. Should the power factor, as metered
     at the point of delivery, not be maintained within such limits, Deseret shall notify the
     Member and request that the power factor be corrected. If the Member has not begun
     corrective action at the end of 90 days, corrective action may be taken and the Member
     shall be obligated to compensate Deseret for all sums expended.

J.   Required Purchase:

     To the extent Member is required by PURPA or other applicable law to purchase power or
     energy ("Required Purchase") from a Qualifying Facility or any other source, other than
     currently existing resources exempted under the Member's Wholesale Power Contract.
     Deseret will charge or allocate to Member any and all losses in revenue or costs (including
     fixed costs) to Deseret that cannot be avoided as a result of such Required Purchase, in a
     manner consistent with Deseret's policy, FERC Order 69 (Docket No. RM79-55), and 45
     Fed. Reg. 12214, 12219 (Feb. 25, 1980). Member must deduct any such losses and costs
     from the price it would otherwise pay for the Required Purchase; payments for the
     Required Purchase must be based on Deseret's then-current avoided cost rates, as
     determined from time to time by Deseret. Member must notify Deseret promptly after
     Member learns about the possibility it may be asked to make a Required Purchase and
     cooperate fully with Deseret in determining the extent and nature of Member's legal
     obligations with respect to a Required Purchase.

     Whenever a Member's Wholesale Power Contract with Deseret provides for supply of
     electricity in a manner which will require service at a voltage level below 138 kV, such
     facilities, when obtained by Deseret, will be provided pursuant to a monthly Excess
     Facilities Charge based on the cost to Deseret for such facilities.

               in full. Deseret shall reimburse any amount determined to have been correctly
               disputed, with a simple interest charge thereon equal to one percent (1%) per month
               on the reimbursed amount, pro-rated by days, until such amount owed, including
               interest, is paid in full.

       2.      Late Payment Charge

               A monthly late payment charge will be added by Deseret when payments are not
               received within five (5) days after the end of the month in which the invoice is
               mailed to the Member. In the event the Bills are not rendered by the twentieth
               (20th) day of the month the final due date shall be fifteen (15) days after the date
               on which the bill is issued. If the scheduled payment date falls on other than a
               business day, the payment is due on the next normal business day. The late
               payment charge for each day beyond the final due date shall be computed as the
               simple interest on the unpaid balance at a rate of 1 percent per month, pro-rated by
               days. The late payment charge will be added to the billing amount for the next
               month. Payments will be credited against the most delinquent charges.

       This Renewal Wholesale Power Contract (“Renewal Agreement”) is entered into

effective the 1st day of January, 2017 (“Effective Date”) between Deseret Generation &

Transmission Co-operative (“Deseret”), a corporation organized and existing under the

laws of the State of Utah, and Garkane Energy Cooperative Inc. (“Member”), a non-profit

corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Utah. Deseret and

Member are sometimes referred to collectively in this Renewal Agreement as the “parties,”

or, individually, as a “party.” This Renewal Agreement supersedes and replaces the

“Wholesale Power Contract” dated as of April 1, 1996 between Deseret and Member (the

“Original Agreement”).

       WHEREAS, Deseret is a wholesale electric generation and transmission

cooperative that owns and operates the Bonanza power plant located near Vernal, Utah,

owns an interest in the Hunter II power plant located near Castledale, Utah, and owns

transmission facilities and rights and otherwise purchases or obtains electric power and

energy for the purpose, among others, of supplying electric power and energy to its

members;
        WHEREAS, Member is an electrical distribution cooperative that operates a

distribution system and other facilities for the purpose, among others, of providing retail

electrical services to its member-owners;

       WHEREAS, Member and Deseret are parties to that certain Resource Integration

Agreement dated as of April 1, 1996 (the “Original RIA Agreement”);

       WHEREAS, this Renewal Agreement is entered into in contemplation of and as a

part of a renewal and extension of the Original Agreement among Deseret and certain of its

members;

       WHEREAS, Deseret has entered into or may enter into agreements for the sale of

electric power and energy similar in form to this Renewal Agreement with other Renewing

Members of Deseret; and

       WHEREAS, Deseret desires to sell and Member desires to purchase electric power

and energy from Deseret on the terms and conditions herein set forth.

       NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual undertakings herein contained,

the parties hereto agree as follows:

       1.       DEFINITIONS.

       As used herein, the following capitalized terms shall have the meaning set forth

       below:

                (a)   “Deseret POD” shall mean and include: (i) any point of delivery that is

identified, as of the Effective Date, on a valid Schedule “B” to an Original Agreement, as

specified in the Exhibit “B-Renewal” to the Renewal Rate “A”, up to the capacity of Deseret

to effect deliveries of power and energy at such POD as of the Effective Date of this
 Renewal Agreement, utilizing all existing available capacity of Deseret transmission

facilities and/or contractual transmission rights as of such date; (ii) a point of delivery that

is deemed acceptable to Deseret by action of the Board of Trustees of Deseret and is

included in written agreement or schedule executed by both Member and Deseret (a “New

POD”), provided, however, that any designation of a New POD shall result in additional

charges as provided in this Renewal Agreement.

               (b)    “Environmental Impacts” include costs, expenses, fees, reduced or

lost revenues, and other consequences of Environmental Compliance (as defined below)

arising from actions reasonably taken by Deseret, the Deseret Board of Trustees, any

federal, state or local regulatory authority, any recognized environmental attributes trading

exchange, organized power market, transmission provider or authority. “Environmental

Compliance” means actions that are reasonably prudent or necessary to monitor or

address any applicable environmental laws or requirements relating to the ownership,

operation, maintenance, disposal, remediation, reclamation, or control of any portion of

Deseret’s electric generation, transmission, communication, fuel supply, systems or other

corporate assets.

               (c)    “Large Industrial and Commercial Load” shall mean and include any

retail load or loads which are under common ownership or control, or which operate, in the

reasonable judgment of Deseret, as a related logical unit, and which, in the aggregate is

reasonably anticipated to exceed the Large Load Threshold in any calendar month during

 defined in Section 21 below) of this Renewal Agreement, alter and/or modify the Large Load

Threshold by action of the majority of voting members of the Deseret Board of Trustees. A

load that, as of the Effective Date, formed any material portion of a load served pursuant to

a Negotiated Special Rate Agreement shall continue to be included and treated as a Large

Industrial and Commercial Load for purposes hereof (regardless of the peak load demand)

through the termination of any current term of any Negotiated Contract Rate Agreement

pertaining to such load(s), and thereafter to the extent such load(s) continue to form any

material portion of a Large Industrial and Commercial Load as otherwise defined

hereunder. Any retail load(s) which, through growth, change in character or operation, or

              (c)    Deseret’s Board of Trustees may adjust, establish, and promulgate

the rates and charges set forth in Wholesale Rate Schedule C to reflect changes which, in

the sole discretion of Deseret’s Board of Trustees, are not inconsistent with Deseret’s

market based rate making authority as it may be established from time to time.
                 (d)   Notwithstanding any other provision of this Renewal Agreement, in no

event prior to the end of the Initial Term hereof shall Deseret’s Board of Trustees adjust,

establish, or promulgate any rate for Tier 2 Demand or Energy (as set forth in Renewal Rate

“A”) in excess of the amount(s) provided in the form of the attached Renewal Rate “A”

attached to this Renewal Agreement as said rate is set forth as of the Effective Date of this

Renewal Agreement.

                (e)   Notwithstanding any other provision of this Renewal Agreement,

Member hereby agrees that the Rebate Methodology heretofore approved for Deseret

member rates is hereby superseded and replaced. Member hereby agrees that Deseret’s

Board of Trustees may, from time to time, declare and pay rebates on account of rates to

members in accordance with the provisions of Exhibit C-4 through C-6 (the “Extension

Term Rebate Schedules”) to the Renewal Rate “A”. In no event shall the amounts and/or

terms of the rebates set forth on the Extension Term Rebate Schedules be altered or

amended prior to the end of the Initial Term hereof. Without limiting the foregoing, Member

hereby acknowledges and agrees that Deseret may, from time to time, declare and

distribute any capital patronage rotation as the Board of Trustees of Deseret may

determine, in its sole discretion, without respect to and regardless of whether or to what

extent any payment of any rebate is paid pursuant to the Extension Term Rebate Schedules

or otherwise.

                (f)   Notwithstanding any other provision of this Renewal Agreement, prior

to the end of the Initial Term hereof, in no event shall Deseret’s Board of Trustees adjust,
 establish or promulgate an Annual Facility Charge for Member in excess of the Facility

Charge provided In the Renewal Rate “A”.

              (g)    Any rate adjustment other than or in excess of the adjustments

permitted under paragraphs 5.b, 5.c., 5.d, or 5.e, above, must be accepted and approved in

writing by Member; based on a vote of Member's Board of Directors.

              (h)    Any revisions in rates shall become effective not less than thirty (30)

days after Deseret has sent notice to Member of a rate revision approved by Deseret's

Board of Trustees and consistent with the terms of this Renewal Agreement.

       6.     METER READINGS AND PAYMENT OF BILLS.

       Deseret shall cause meters to be read at least monthly. Electric power and energy

furnished hereunder shall be paid for monthly at the office of Deseret in South Jordan,

Utah, or at such other place as Deseret may hereafter specify, under terms and conditions

as stated in the applicable rate schedule.

       7.     EXTENSION AND CONTINUATION OF RESOURCE INTEGRATION

AGREEEMENT.

       Subject to the provisions of this Section 7, the Original RIA Agreement between

Member and Deseret is and shall continue in full force and effect in accordance with the

terms thereof for so long as Member’s Renewal Agreement remains in force and effect, as if

this Renewal Agreement were deemed to be an amendment of the Original Agreement for

purposes of the provisions of Paragraph 6 of the Original RIA Agreement.
               (a)     Extended Term of RIA. Notwithstanding any provision of the Original

RIA Agreement, Section 6 of the Original RIA Agreement is hereby amended and

superseded and restated to read in its entirety as follows:

              6.      Term. This Resource Integration Agreement shall remain in full

              force and effect so long as Member’s wholesale power contract with

              Deseret, or, in the event of a Renewal Wholesale Power Contract, and

              such Renewal Wholesale Power Contract with Deseret, in either case

              as such agreement(s) may be amended, remains in full force and

              effect. Member may not terminate this Agreement under any

              circumstances unless:

              (i)     Deseret makes a change to the structure, terms or conditions

              of Wholesale Rate “A” or Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule “A” (as

              the case may be), not agreed to by the Member, that results in an

              increase in the individual Member’s rate, in excess of adjustments to

              rates and charges authorized pursuant to the terms of the Renewal

              Wholesale Power Contract between Member and Deseret;

              (ii)    a creditor of Deseret properly declares an Event of Default

              under Deseret’s 1996 debt restructuring agreement which is not cured

              by Deseret; or

              (iii)   Deseret is dissolved, merged into another entity without the

              consent of Member or declared insolvent by a court of competent

              jurisdiction.
               Upon any termination of this Resource Integration Agreement,

              Member shall not be eligible to receive service under Wholesale Rate

              “A”, or Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule “A.”

              (b)    Revision to Credited Costs for Integrated Resources. Commencing

effective January 1, 2026, (the “Member Resource Date”) and notwithstanding any other

provision of the Original RIA Agreement (but without modifying any restriction or prohibition

against member owned resources or third party power purchased pursuant to this Renewal

Agreement), Member shall be solely responsible, at its cost and risk, for all costs, fees,

charges, liabilities, and other expenses associated with or arising out of the ownership,

operation, maintenance, licensing, re-licensing of any member owned resources (including

any resource referred to in Section 2.b(i)). Deseret shall not credit nor charge Member for

any amounts of power or energy delivered from any member owned resources from and

after the Member Resource Date, except and solely to the extent that deliveries of power

and energy received by Member from such Member resource(s) may diminish the billing

demand and/or billing energy received from Deseret pursuant to this Renewal Agreement

from and after the Member Resource Date.

       8.     METER TESTING AND BILLING ADJUSTMENT.

       Deseret shall test and calibrate meters by comparison with accurate standards at

intervals of approximately twelve (12) months. Upon request, Deseret shall notify Member

in advance of the time of any meter test so that a representative of Member may be present

at such meter test. Deseret shall also make special meter tests at any time at Member's

request. The costs of all tests shall be borne by Deseret; provided, however, that if any
 special meter test made at Member's request shall disclose that the meters are recording

accurately, Member shall reimburse Deseret for the cost of such test. Meters registering

not more than one half of one percent (0.5 %) above or below normal shall be deemed to

be accurate. The readings of any meter which shall have been disclosed by test to be

inaccurate shall be corrected for the ninety (90) days previous to such test in accordance

with the percentage of inaccuracy found by such test. If any meter shall fail to register for

any period, Member and Deseret shall cooperate in good faith to estimate the amount of

energy furnished during such period.

       9.     RIGHT OF ACCESS.

       Duly authorized representatives of either party hereto shall be permitted to enter the

premises of the other party hereto at all reasonable times in order to carry out the

provisions hereof.

       10.    CONTINUITY OF SERVICE.

       Deseret shall use reasonable diligence to provide a constant and uninterrupted

supply of electric power and energy hereunder. If the supply of electric power and energy

shall fail or be interrupted, or become defective through act of God or a public enemy, or

because of accident, labor troubles, or any other cause beyond the control of Deseret,

Deseret shall not be liable therefor or for damages caused thereby.

       11.    REGULATORY APPROVALS AND OTHER ACTIONS.

       This Renewal Agreement shall be subject to any necessary regulatory approvals. At

Deseret's request, Member will use its best efforts to obtain or assist in obtaining any

approvals or orders that may be necessary that may be from any regulatory authority in
 connection with the approval, implementation or enforcement of this Renewal Agreement.

Member shall also take such further or additional steps or actions as may reasonably be

requested by Deseret to assist in implementing and operating under this Renewal

Agreement. Other than as specifically set forth herein: (i) except with the written consent

of the other party, neither Deseret nor Member, nor any person or entity acting or purporting

to act on behalf or with the authority of either, may change or adjust the rates, term, or any

other provision contained in this Renewal Agreement; (ii) neither Deseret nor Member, nor

any person or entity acting or purporting to act on behalf or with the authority of either, may

seek or request from, or support any request to, any agency, authority, person or entity

exercising or purporting to exercise any regulatory or ratemaking rights or authority, for any

change or adjustment to the rates, term, or any other provision of this Renewal Agreement;

and (iii) to the fullest extent permitted by law, no person, entity, agency or authority

exercising or purporting to exercise any regulatory or ratemaking rights or authority,

whether on its own motion or at the request of any person or entity, may change or adjust,

or seek to change or adjust, the rates, term, or any other provision contained in this

Renewal Agreement, whether pursuant to a "just and reasonable" standard of review or any

other standard of review, except to the limited extent such agency or authority may have an

indefeasible statutory right to adjust the rates or other provisions of this Renewal

Agreement to the extent they are determined to be contrary to the public interest.

       Without limiting the foregoing, absent the agreement of all Parties to the proposed

change, the standard of review for changes to Sections 1 through 18 of this Renewal

Agreement, including any term or provision set forth in the Exhibits hereto, proposed by a
 party, a non-party or the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission acting sua sponte shall be

the “public interest” standard of review set forth in United Gas Pipe Line Co. v. Mobile Gas

Service Corp., 350 U.S. 332 (1956) and Federal Power Commission v. Sierra Pacific Power

Co., 350 U.S. 348 (1956) (the “Mobile-Sierra” doctrine) and clarified in Morgan Stanley

Capital Group Inc. v. Public Util. Dist. No. 1 of Snohomish, 554 U.S. 527 (2008) and NRG

Power Mktg LLC v. Maine Pub. Util. Comm’n, 558 U.S. 165 (2010).

       12.    EFFECTIVE DATE – CONDITION TO EFFECTIVENESS.

       Upon execution by both parties, this Renewal Agreement shall become effective

and binding effective no later than January 1, 2017, subject to any necessary regulatory

approvals, and subject further to the following:

              (a)    Notwithstanding anything in this Renewal Agreement, this Renewal

Agreement shall not become effective unless and until, on or before March 31, 2017, at

least four (4) Renewing Members, (including Member) shall have executed and delivered a

Renewal Agreement in substantially similar form and substance as this Renewal

Agreement, with variations reflecting only specific items set forth in Section 13 of a

particular Renewing Member’s Renewal Agreement pertaining to the executing member

and approved by Deseret’s Board of Trustees, as well as other items related to: items listed

by each Renewing Member in its attached Exhibit “A-Renewal” to Renewal Rate “A”

(Member Exempt Resource(s)); and items listed by each Renewing Member in its attached

Exhibit “B-Renewal” to Renewal Rate “A” (Member specified POD’s), to the Renewal

Agreement executed by each such Renewing Member.
                 (b)   Without limiting the foregoing, this Renewal Agreement shall become

effective upon Deseret’s Board of Trustees’ express action authorizing execution hereof on

behalf of Deseret, but only after sufficient number of Renewing Members have executed

and delivered a Renewal Agreement.

         13.    EFFECT ON CERTAIN AGREEMENTS; PHASEOUT AND TERMINATION OF
                1993 TRANSMISSION SERVICE AGREEMENT.

A.   Fredonia Transmission Agreement to Remain in Effect through December 31, 2025. That

     certain Transmission Agreement (“Fredonia TSA”) dated as of July 21, 1993 between

     Deseret and Garkane providing, among other things, for transmission service charge (the

     “Fredonia Transmission Wheel”) to be paid by Deseret shall remain in effect and Deseret

     shall continue to pay the Fredonia Transmission Wheel through December 31, 2025 (the

     “TSA Termination Date”), subject to the following. Notwithstanding any provision of the

     Fredonia TSA, Deseret shall pay to Garkane in full and complete satisfaction of all

     obligations for payments on account of the Fredonia Transmission Wheel the fixed sum of

     $475,000 per year (paid monthly on a prorated monthly basis) beginning effective July 1,

     2016 through the TSA Termination Date. From and after the TSA Termination Date, no

     further payments will be made to Garkane on account of any deliveries or transmission

     charges.

 B. Kanab and Twin Cities Charges Discontinued. Reference is made to the following:

         That certain Acquired Retail Load Rider dated effective August 31, 2004 between
          Deseret and Garkane providing, among other things, for the assessment and collection
          of an Annual Acquisition Adjustment (the “Kanab Acquisition Charge”);

         That certain Amendment to Wholesale Power Contract dated as of June 2009 between
          Deseret and Garkane providing, among other things, for an additional Service Fee For
          Acquired Load (the “Twin Cities Service Fee”);
      The Kanab Acquisition Charge, and the Twin Cities Service Fee are aggregated for purposes

     of this Section 13 and referred to collectively, in aggregate, as the “Garkane Additional

     Consideration.” Beginning with deliveries to Garkane for service to all loads described for

     service under Renewal Rate Schedule “A” (attached hereto as Schedule “A-Renewal”),

     Garkane will transition from Deseret’s Wholesale Rate “A” (including the Kanab Acquisition

     Charge and the Twin Cities Service Fee) to begin taking service under the Renewal

     Wholesale Rate Schedule “A”. As part of the transition, and in consideration of this

     Renewal Agreement between Deseret and Garkane, Deseret and Garkane agree as

     follows: Garkane shall pay and/or collect, and Deseret will pay and/or collect, as the case

     may be, each component of the Garkane Additional Consideration in addition to all other

     charges set forth in Renewal Rate Schedule “A” up to the Effective Date of the said

     Renewal Rate Schedule “A”. From and after the Effective Date of the Renewal Rate

     Schedule “A”, Garkane will not pay and Deseret will not collect any amount(s) as Kanab

     Acquisition Charge or Twin Cities Service Fee. The parties agree that Deseret may prepare

     and file, as appropriate additional addenda and/or service schedules to Renewal Rate

     Schedule “A” to reflect the foregoing.

       14.    CONTRIBUTIONS IN AID OF CONSTRUCTION.

       Beginning from and after the first day of the Renewal Term following the Initial Term

of this Renewal Agreement, Deseret shall reserve and set aside for the benefit of any given

Renewing Member an amount (an “Industrial Distribution Facility Reserve”), equal to

twenty percent (20%) of the positive difference, if any, between:
               (a)     the revenue collected by Deseret each year on account of sales to

that specific Renewing Member of power and energy for service to each Large Industrial

and Commercial Load that is provided pursuant to a mutually negotiated Large Customer

Agreement with that specific Member reflecting the highest marginally-priced power and

energy provided to such Large Industrial and Commercial Load during each billing period

under the terms of each Large Customer Agreement;

              minus

              (b)     the revenue that would have been received by Deseret on account of

such equivalent quantity of power and energy had it been sold to a wholesale purchaser at

rates equal to the Renewal Rate “A” rates and charges then in effect.


The funds set aside as the Industrial Distribution Facility Reserve for any given Renewing

Member shall be disbursed as follows: first, upon request of that specific Renewing

Member for reimbursement of Verified Industrial Facility Expenditures, Deseret shall pay to

that specific Renewing Member as a non-reimbursable contribution in aid of construction,

unreimbursed amount(s) of such Verified Industrial Facility Expenditures up to the

undistributed balance of the Industrial Distribution Facility Reserve for that specific

Renewing Member as of the first day of the calendar year in which such request is received,

such disbursement of funds from the Reserve to be made on a first-in-first out basis from

the undisbursed funds then held in reserve; and second, after ten (10) full calendar years

                        RENEWAL WHOLESALE POWER CONTRACT

                                         BETWEEN

                DESERET GENERATION & TRANSMISSION CO-OPERATIVE

                                            AND

                     BRIDGER VALLEY ELECTRIC ASSOCIATION, INC.

       This Renewal Wholesale Power Contract (“Renewal Agreement”) is entered into

effective the 1st day of January, 2017 (“Effective Date”) between Deseret Generation &

Transmission Co-operative (“Deseret”), a corporation organized and existing under the

laws of the State of Utah, and Bridger Valley Electric Association, Inc. (“Member”), a non-

profit corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Wyoming. Deseret

and Member are sometimes referred to collectively in this Renewal Agreement as the

“parties,” or, individually, as a “party.” This Renewal Agreement supersedes and replaces

the “Wholesale Power Contract” dated as of April 1, 1996 between Deseret and Member

(the “Original Agreement”).

       WHEREAS, Deseret is a wholesale electric generation and transmission cooperative

that owns and operates the Bonanza power plant located near Vernal, Utah, owns an

interest in the Hunter II power plant located near Castledale, Utah, and owns transmission

facilities and rights and otherwise purchases or obtains electric power and energy for the

purpose, among others, of supplying electric power and energy to its members;

       WHEREAS, Member is an electrical distribution cooperative that operates a

distribution system and other facilities for the purpose, among others, of providing retail

electrical services to its member-owners;
        WHEREAS, Member and Deseret are parties to that certain Resource Integration

Agreement dated as of April 1, 1996 (the “Original RIA Agreement”);

       WHEREAS, this Renewal Agreement is entered into in contemplation of and as a

part of a renewal and extension of the Original Agreement among Deseret and certain of its

members;

       WHEREAS, Deseret has entered into or may enter into agreements for the sale of

electric power and energy similar in form to this Renewal Agreement with other Renewing

Members of Deseret; and

       WHEREAS, Deseret desires to sell and Member desires to purchase electric power

and energy from Deseret on the terms and conditions herein set forth.

       NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual undertakings herein contained,

the parties hereto agree as follows:

        1.       DEFINITIONS.

       As used herein, the following capitalized terms shall have the meaning set forth

       below:

                (a)   “Deseret POD” shall mean and include: (i) any point of delivery that is

identified, as of the Effective Date, on a valid Schedule “B” to an Original Agreement, as

specified in the Exhibit “B-Renewal” to the Renewal Rate “A”, up to the capacity of Deseret

to effect deliveries of power and energy at such POD as of the Effective Date of this

Renewal Agreement, utilizing all existing available capacity of Deseret transmission

facilities and/or contractual transmission rights as of such date; (ii) a point of delivery that

is deemed acceptable to Deseret by action of the Board of Trustees of Deseret and is
 included in written agreement or schedule executed by both Member and Deseret (a “New

POD”), provided, however, that any designation of a New POD shall result in additional

charges as provided in this Renewal Agreement.

              (b)    “Environmental Impacts” include costs, expenses, fees, reduced or

lost revenues, and other consequences of Environmental Compliance (as defined below)

arising from actions reasonably taken by Deseret, the Deseret Board of Trustees, any

federal, state or local regulatory authority, any recognized environmental attributes trading

exchange, organized power market, transmission provider or authority. “Environmental

Compliance” means actions that are reasonably prudent or necessary to monitor or

address any applicable environmental laws or requirements relating to the ownership,

operation, maintenance, disposal, remediation, reclamation, or control of any portion of

Deseret’s electric generation, transmission, communication, fuel supply, systems or other

corporate assets.

              (c)    “Large Industrial and Commercial Load” shall mean and include any

retail load or loads which are under common ownership or control, or which operate, in the

reasonable judgment of Deseret, as a related logical unit, and which, in the aggregate is

reasonably anticipated to exceed the Large Load Threshold in any calendar month during

the term of this Renewal Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Board of Trustees

of Deseret may, effective beginning any time or from time to time after the Initial Term (as

defined in Section 21 below) of this Renewal Agreement, alter and/or modify the Large Load

Threshold by action of the majority of voting members of the Deseret Board of Trustees. A

load that, as of the Effective Date, formed any material portion of a load served pursuant to
 a Negotiated Special Rate Agreement shall continue to be included and treated as a Large

Industrial and Commercial Load for purposes hereof (regardless of the peak load demand)

through the termination of any current term of any Negotiated Contract Rate Agreement

pertaining to such load(s), and thereafter to the extent such load(s) continue to form any

material portion of a Large Industrial and Commercial Load as otherwise defined

hereunder. Any retail load(s) which, through growth, change in character or operation, or

any combination thereof is reasonably anticipated to exceed the threshold size set forth

herein shall be deemed and treated as a Large Industrial and Commercial Load beginning

with the first day of the first calendar month in which the load (or aggregated load) is

reasonably anticipated to exceed the threshold. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in no event

shall any retail load which Deseret, in its reasonable judgment, deems to be primarily

agricultural, governmental, or charitable in nature, be included in any aggregation or

otherwise be deemed to constitute a Large Industrial and Commercial Load.

              (d)     “Large Load Threshold” shall mean 2.5 MW peak demand, or such

other quantity (in MW) (commencing after the Initial Term) that: (i) Deseret’s Board of

Trustees shall approve from time to time during the term of this Renewal Agreement; and

(ii) all creditors of Deseret under the ORA have approved in writing during the term of the

ORA as the same may be modified or extended; and (iii) would not result in any default of

any written covenant, agreement or instrument to which Deseret or its subsidiary is a party.

              (e)     “ORA” shall mean that certain Obligations Restructuring Agreement

dated as of October 16, 1996 among Deseret, Blue Mountain Energy, Inc., National Rural

Utilities Cooperative Finance Corporation, and National Cooperative Services Corporation,
 as the same has been or may be modified and amended from time to time in writing

executed by Deseret and authorized by the Board of Trustees of Deseret.

                  (f)   “Member Resource” shall mean and include those permitted

resources under the Member’s Original RIA Agreement that are not included in either any

SLPP Resource or any IPP Resource.

                  (g)   “Renewal Rate “A”” shall mean the Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule “A”

attached hereto as Attachment 1, including all Exhibits thereto, all of which is hereby incorporated by

this reference.

                  (h)   “Renewing Member” means and includes each member of Deseret

that is a rural electric distribution cooperative that, as of January 1, 2016, is party to an

agreement with Deseret similar in form and substance to the Original Agreement, is a party

to a valid and effective Original RIA Agreement; and which executes and delivers a Renewal

Agreement as set forth in Section 11 below.

                  (i)   “Verified Industrial Facility Expenditures” means actual, reasonable,

and unavoidable expenditures by a Renewing Member incurred on or after the Effective

Date of this Renewal Agreement, supported by adequate substantiated documentary

support, for necessary improvements, upgrades, and/or construction of electric

distribution and/or transmission facilities on Member’s distribution system that, in the

reasonable opinion of both Member and Deseret, are prudent and useful for continued

service to one or more retail customer loads served under one or more Large Customer

Agreements (as defined in section 2.b.(iv)) as set forth pursuant to the terms of this

Renewal Agreement.
               (j)    Wholesale Rate Schedule “C” shall mean Deseret’s Wholesale Rate

“C” as previously promulgated and adopted by Deseret pursuant to market-based

ratemaking authority granted by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, as the same

may be modified, adjusted, promulgated, replaced, or superseded from time to time by the

action of Deseret’s governing board.

         2.    REQUIREMENTS CONTRACT.

              (a)    Beginning immediately upon the Effective Date, Member shall receive,

and Deseret shall deliver to Member, electric power and service pursuant to this Renewal

Agreement, and deliveries pursuant to the Original Agreement shall thereupon cease.

Deseret shall sell and deliver to Member (at the Points of Delivery specified in paragraph 3

of this Renewal Agreement), and Member shall purchase and receive from Deseret, all

electric power and energy which Member requires to operate the Member’s system and

serve the Member’s retail consumer-members’ requirements, to the extent Deseret has the

power, energy and necessary facilities available, excepting only the power or energy

generated by or acquired from Member’s Exempt Resources as specified in paragraph 2.b.,

below.

              (b)    Notwithstanding Member’s all-requirements obligation as set forth in

paragraph 2(a) above, and without limiting the effect or provisions of any Resource

Integration Agreement or similar agreement between Deseret and Member (as the same

may be amended, modified, or extended, an “Integration Agreement”), and as applicable,

Member may acquire and/or utilize the following amounts of power and/or energy

generated by the following sources (“Member’s Exempt Resources”):
                       (i)     Generation and Purchased Power Resources. Member may

acquire and/or utilize electric power and energy generated by or purchased from the

generation and purchased power resources specified for such Member in paragraph 1 of

Exhibit “A-Renewal” to the Renewal Rate “A” (“Generation and Purchased Power

Resources”), up to the maximum amounts of capacity and the maximum amounts of

energy specified in paragraph 1 of said Exhibit “A-Renewal” (or, in the case of nameplate

capacity specified in said Exhibit “A-Renewal,” no more than the nameplate capacity

and/or energy associated with the hourly output up to such capacity in any given hour).

Without Deseret’s prior written approval, Member will not receive or purchase more than

the minimum power and energy requirements specified under any contracts or tariffs in

force as of January 1, 1996, for Generation and Purchased Power Resources specified in

paragraph 1 of Exhibit “A-Renewal” and will not change, amend, renew or extend any

contract or any contractual obligations relating to any such Generation and Purchased

Power Resources without the approval of Deseret’s Board of Trustees. Member will not

construct, operate or purchase power from any other or future resources (including

resources exempted under this paragraph 2(b) absent future written agreement between

Deseret and Member. Nothing in this paragraph 2(b)(i) is intended to limit or affect the

ability of Member to produce or acquire, or any obligation of Deseret to take, schedule or

use, the output of hydroelectric facilities, to the extent specified in an Integration

Agreement.

                      (ii)    SLIP Resources. Member may acquire and/or utilize electric

power and energy allocated and made available to Member by Western Area Power
 Administration or any successor ("Western") and furnished by the Salt Lake City Area

Integrated Projects or successor resources ("SLIP Resources”) up to a maximum of (i)

Member's seasonal entitlements to energy and capacity under Amendment No. 1 to

Member's existing firm power supply contract with Western, as specified in paragraph 2 of

Exhibit "A-Renewal" to the Renewal Rate “A”; and (ii) Member's monthly entitlements

(consistent with the seasonal entitlements referenced in clause (i) above) established in

accordance with Exhibit A to Member's contract with Western, as said Exhibit A may be

amended from time to time. In the event Member's allocations of seasonal energy and

capacity generated by SLIP Resources are hereafter modified through an amended or

successor contract with Western, Member may purchase up to the modified seasonal

allocations; however, without Deseret's written consent, Member may not purchase more

than Member's original allocations of post-1989 seasonal capacity and energy, as specified

in paragraph 2 of said Exhibit “A-Renewal” to the Renewal Rate “A”. Without the advance

written consent of Deseret, Member may not (i) purchase energy or capacity generated by

non-SLIP Resources offered by Western or others on a pass-through basis or otherwise; or

(ii) purchase laid-off, exchanged, excess or emergency resources or allocations of SLIP or

non-SLIP resources offered by Western, other preference customers of Western, or

otherwise. Deseret and, Member will cooperate to utilize all SLIP Resources and other

resources available from Western so as to maximize benefits to Deseret's system and

Deseret's members.

                     (iii)   IPA Resources. Member may acquire and/or utilize electric

power and energy available to Member under (i) the Power Sales Contract (the "IPA
 Contract") with the Intermountain Power Agency ("IPA") dated September 28, 1978, and (ii)

the Excess Power Sales Agreement (the "Excess Agreement") among Deseret,

Intermountain Consumer Power Association, certain California Purchasers, and others

dated December 1, 1980, as specified in paragraph 3 of Exhibit “A-Renewal” to Renewal

Rate “A”. Subject to the prior written approval of Deseret, Member may enter into renewal

and/or extensions of the IPA Contract and/or the Excess Agreement (collectively the “IPA

Renewal Contracts”). Member shall exercise solely in such manner as directed by Deseret,

all rights, powers, and remedies which the Member has or may have under the IPA

Contract, the Excess Agreement, and any IPA Renewal Contracts, as any of them has been

or may be amended, modified, supplemented, renewed, or extended. Without the prior

written consent of Deseret, Member shall not amend, modify, supplement, renew, extend,

or terminate the IPA Contract or the Excess Agreement, (or any IPA Renewal Contract), or

consent to the same. Member shall not modify its Excess Entitlement Share (as defined in

the Excess Agreement and/or any IPA Renewal Agreement) or otherwise recall any power or

energy that has been laid off to the California Purchasers under the Excess Agreement

and/or any IPA Renewal Agreement without the prior written consent of Deseret. Any power

or energy recalled and purchased by Member under the IPA Contract, the Excess

Agreement, or any IPA Renewal Contract shall be pooled for all purposes with all other

power and energy owned or purchased by Deseret. Deseret shall have full authority over all

power and energy purchased under the IPA Contract, the Excess Agreement, and/or the IPA

Renewal Contracts for all purposes, including pooling, scheduling, and economic

dispatch. Payments for any electric power and energy purchased under the IPA Contract,
 the Excess Agreement, and any IPA Renewal Contracts shall be paid directly to IPA by

Deseret on behalf of Member. Nothing contained herein shall constitute or be deemed to

constitute or require a sale, assignment, transfer, or other disposition by Member, to

Deseret or any other person, of the Member's power and energy entitlement under the IPA

Contract, the Excess Agreement, or the IPA Renewal Contracts. Notwithstanding any

language to the contrary found in this Renewal Agreement or in any Integration Agreement,

should Deseret default in the payment of monies owed to IPA on behalf of Member and fail

to cure such default promptly upon notice (a "Deseret IPA Default"), then Deseret shall

forfeit its above-described right to direct Member's actions with respect to the IPA

that specific Renewing Member of power and energy for service to each Large Industrial

and Commercial Load that is provided pursuant to a mutually negotiated Large Customer

Agreement with that specific Member reflecting the highest marginally-priced power and

energy provided to such Large Industrial and Commercial Load during each billing period

under the terms of each Large Customer Agreement;

              minus

such equivalent quantity of power and energy had it been sold to a wholesale purchaser at

rates equal to the Renewal Rate “A” rates and charges then in effect.



The funds set aside as the Industrial Distribution Facility Reserve for any given Renewing

Member shall be disbursed as follows: first, upon request of that specific Renewing

Member for reimbursement of Verified Industrial Facility Expenditures, Deseret shall pay to

that specific Renewing Member as a non-reimbursable contribution in aid of construction,

unreimbursed amount(s) of such Verified Industrial Facility Expenditures up to the
 undistributed balance of the Industrial Distribution Facility Reserve for that specific

Renewing Member as of the first day of the calendar year in which such request is received,

such disbursement of funds from the Reserve to be made on a first-in-first out basis from

the undisbursed funds then held in reserve; and second, after ten (10) full calendar years

following the date(s) on which funds are set aside into the Industrial Distribution Facility

Reserve on account of any Large Industrial and Commercial Load, any portion of such

vintage funds remaining undisbursed may be released and retained by Deseret for general

corporate purposes.

                      BRIDGER VALLEY ELECTRIC ASSOCIATION, INC.

This Wholesale Power Contract ("Agreement") is entered into effective the 1st day of April, 1996
between Deseret Generation & Transmission Co-operative ("Deseret"), a corporation organized and
existing under the laws of the State of Utah, and Bridger Valley Electric Association, Inc. ("Member"),
a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the State of Wyoming. This Agreement
supersedes and replaces the "Wholesale Power Contract - Federated Cooperative" dated October 10,
 1980, as amended by the "1990 Amendment to Wholesale Power Contract" dated January 7, 1991,
between Deseret and Member.

WHEREAS, Deseret is a wholesale electric generation and transmission cooperative that currently
operates the Bonanza power plant, owns an interest in the Hunter II power plant, owns transmission
facilities and rights and otherwise purchases or obtains electric power and energy for the purpose,
among others, of supplying electric power and energy to its members;

WHEREAS, Member is an electrical distribution cooperative that operates a distribution system and
other facilities for the purpose, among others, of providing retail electrical services to its member-
owners;

WHEREAS, this Agreement is entered into in contemplation of and as a part of a general workout
and restructuring among Deseret and its creditors ("Workout");

WHEREAS, Deseret has entered or may enter into agreements for the sale of electric power and
energy similar in form to this Agreement with other members of Deseret; and

WHEREAS, Deseret desires to sell and Member desires to purchase electric power and energy from
Deseret on the terms and conditions herein set forth.

NOW THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual undertakings herein contained, the parties
hereto agree as follows:

                                                  1.   REQUIREMENTS CONTRACT

                                                        a.      Deseret shall sell and deliver to
Member (at the Points of Delivery specified in paragraph 2 of this Agreement) and Member shall
purchase and receive from Deseret, all electric power and energy which Member requires for serving
its retail consumer-members' requirements and operation of Member's system, to the extent Deseret
has the power, energy and necessary facilities available, excepting only the power or energy generated
by or acquired from Member's Exempt Resources as specified in paragraph 1.b., below.

                                                    b.     Notwithstanding     Member's       all-
requirements obligation as set forth in paragraph 1.a., above, and without limiting the effect or
provisions of any Resource Integration Agreement or similar agreement between Deseret and
Member ("Integration Agreement"), if and as applicable, Member may acquire and/or utilize the
following amounts of power and/or energy generated by the following sources ("Member's Exempt
Resources"):

(1)Generation and Purchased Power Resources. Member may acquire and/or utilize electric power
and energy generated by or purchased from the generation and purchased power resources specified
in paragraph 1 of Schedule "A" attached hereto ("Generation and Purchased Power Resources"), up
to the maximum amounts of capacity ("Maximum Exempt Capacity") and the maximum amounts of
energy ("Maximum Exempt Energy") specified in paragraph 1 of said Schedule "A". Without
Deseret's prior written approval, Member will not receive or purchase more than the minimum power
 and energy requirements specified under any contracts or tariffs in force as of January 1, 1996, for
Generation and Purchased Power Resources specified in paragraph 1 of Schedule "A" and will not
change, amend, renew or extend any contract or any contractual obligations relating to any such
Generation and Purchased Power Resources without the approval of Deseret's Board of Trustees.
Member will not construct, operate or purchase power from any other or future resources (including
resources exempted under this paragraph 1.b.) absent future written agreement between Deseret and
Member. Nothing in this paragraph 1.b.(1) is intended to limit or affect the ability of Member to
produce or acquire, or any obligation of Deseret to take, schedule or use, the output of hydroelectric
facilities, to the extent specified in an Integration Agreement.

(2)SLIP Resources. Member may acquire and/or utilize electric power and energy allocated and
made available to Member by Western Area Power Administration or any successor ("Western") and
furnished by the Salt Lake City Area Integrated Projects or successor resources ("SLIP Resources"),
up to a maximum of (i) Member's seasonal entitlements to energy and capacity under Amendment
No. 1 to Member's existing firm power supply contract with Western, as specified in paragraph 2 of
Schedule "A" hereto ("Current Entitlements"); and (ii) Member's monthly entitlements (consistent
with the seasonal entitlements referenced in clause (i) above) established in accordance with Exhibit
A to Member's contract with Western, as said Exhibit A may be amended from time to time. In the
event Member's allocations of seasonal energy and capacity generated by SLIP Resources are
hereafter modified through an amended or successor contract with Western, Member may purchase
up to the modified seasonal allocations, but, without Deseret's written consent, in no event more than
Member's original allocations of post-1989 seasonal capacity and energy, as specified in paragraph 2
of Schedule "A" hereto ("Original Allocations"). Without the advance written consent of Deseret,
Member may not (i) purchase energy or capacity generated by non-SLIP Resources offered by
Western or others on a pass-through basis or otherwise; or (ii) purchase laid-off, exchanged, excess
or emergency resources or allocations of SLIP or non-SLIP resources offered by Western, other
preference customers of Western, or otherwise. Deseret and Member will cooperate to utilize all
SLIP Resources and other resources available from Western so as to maximize benefits to Deseret's
system and Deseret's members.

(3)IPA Resources. Member may acquire and/or utilize electric power and energy available to
Member under the Power Sales Contract (the "IPA Contract") with the Intermountain Power Agency
("IPA") dated September 28, 1978 and under the Excess Power Sales Agreement (the "Excess
Agreement") among Deseret, Intermountain Consumer Power Association, certain California
Purchasers, and others dated December 1, 1980, as specified in paragraph 3 of Schedule "A" hereto.
 Member shall exercise solely in such manner as directed by Deseret, all rights, powers, and remedies
which the Member has or may have under the IPA Contract and the Excess Agreement, as either has
been or may be amended, modified, supplemented, renewed, or extended. Without the prior written
consent of Deseret, Member shall not amend, modify, supplement, renew, extend, or terminate the
IPA Contract or the Excess Agreement, or consent to the same. Member shall not modify its Excess
Entitlement Share (as defined in the Excess Agreement) or otherwise recall any power or energy
which has been laid off to the California Purchasers under the Excess Agreement without the prior
written consent of Deseret. Any power or energy recalled and purchased by Member under the IPA
Contract or the Excess Agreement shall be pooled for all purposes with all other power and energy
owned or purchased by Deseret. Deseret shall have full authority over all power and energy
purchased under the IPA Contract or the Excess Agreement for all purposes, including pooling,
 scheduling, and economic dispatch. Payments for any electric power and energy purchased under
the IPA Contract and the Excess Agreement shall be paid directly by Deseret on behalf of Member to
IPA. Nothing contained herein shall constitute or be deemed to constitute or require a sale,
assignment, transfer, or other disposition by the Member to Deseret or any other person of the
Member's power and energy entitlement under the IPA Contract or the Excess Agreement.
Notwithstanding any language to the contrary found in this Agreement or in any Integration
Agreement, should Deseret default in the payment of monies owed to IPA on behalf of Member and
fail to cure such default promptly upon notice (a "Deseret IPA Default"), then Deseret shall forfeit its
above-described right to direct Member's actions with respect to the IPA Contract and the Excess
Agreement. Upon such forfeiture, which remedy is in addition to whatever other remedies may be
available to Member at law or in equity, Member shall have no further obligation to integrate the
power and energy available to it under the IPA Contract and the Excess Agreement as required under
the terms of this Agreement or the Integration Agreement in the absence of such a default.
Furthermore, Deseret agrees to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Member from any claims,
causes of action, costs, damages, and liabilities of any kind arising from or related to a Deseret IPA
Default.


                                                  2.   ELECTRIC CHARACTERISTICS AND
DELIVERY POINT(S).

Electric power and energy to be furnished hereunder shall be delivered under the terms and conditions
contained in the applicable rate schedule to the Points of Delivery specified in Schedule "B" hereto
and shall be alternating current, three phase, sixty cycle. Deseret shall make necessary connections
between the systems of Deseret and Member at the Points of Delivery, with the payments for and
ownership of any such facilities determined in accordance with Deseret's extension policy in effect at
the time of the interconnection. The Points of Delivery, nominal delivery voltage and ownership of
substation and interconnection equipment are specified on Schedule "B" hereto.

                                                  3.   METERING AND WHEELING.

                                                a. Meters and metering equipment shall be
furnished, maintained, and read by Deseret and shall be located at the Points of Delivery on the low
voltage side of such transforming equipment.

                                                b. Deseret shall make all necessary arrangements
and contract for any necessary wheeling of power and energy over the transmission systems of others
between points of interconnection with Deseret and Member's Points of Delivery.

                                                  4.   RATES.

                                                a. Member shall pay Deseret for all electric
power and energy furnished hereunder at the rates and on the terms and conditions set forth in
Wholesale Rate Schedule A (including the Integration Agreement) or Wholesale Rate Schedule B, as
applicable, copies of which are attached hereto as Schedules "C" and "D," respectively. This
Agreement is hereby incorporated into Wholesale Rate Schedule A, Wholesale Rate Schedule B and
 the Integration Agreement; in the event of any inconsistency, the terms of this Agreement shall
control.

                                                   b. Deseret's Board of Trustees may adjust the
rates set forth in Wholesale Rate Schedule A and Wholesale Rate Schedule B only to reflect (i)
changes in Deseret's production costs (exclusive of debt service costs) pro-rated based on the amount
of Deseret's resources utilized to serve member loads compared to Deseret's total resources; (ii)
changes in the costs of the integrated resources of Deseret's members; and (iii) costs of future capital
improvements or capital additions hereafter approved by Deseret's Board of Trustees.

                                                 c. Any rate adjustment other than or in excess of
the adjustments permitted under paragraph 4.b., above, must be accepted and approved in writing by
Member, based on a vote of Member's Board of Directors.

                                                   d. Any revisions in rates shall become effective
not less than thirty (30) days after Deseret has sent notice to Member of a rate revision approved by
Deseret's Board of Trustees and consistent with the terms of this Agreement.

                                                  5. METER READINGS AND PAYMENT OF
BILLS. Deseret shall cause meters to be read at least monthly. Electric power and energy furnished
hereunder shall be paid for monthly at the office of Deseret in Sandy, Utah, or at such other place as
Deseret may hereafter specify, under terms and conditions as stated in the applicable rate schedule.

                                                    6. METER TESTING AND BILLING
ADJUSTMENT. Deseret shall test and calibrate meters by comparison with accurate standards at
intervals of approximately twelve (12) months. Upon request, Deseret shall notify Member in
advance of the time of any meter test so that a representative of Member may be present at such meter
test. Deseret shall also make special meter tests at any time at Member's request. The costs of all
tests shall be borne by Deseret; provided, however, that if any special meter test made at Member's
request shall disclose that the meters are recording accurately, Member shall reimburse Deseret for
the cost of such test. Meters registering not more than one half of one percent (0.5%) above or below
normal shall be deemed to be accurate. The readings of any meter which shall have been disclosed
by test to be inaccurate shall be corrected for the ninety (90) days previous to such test in accordance
with the percentage of inaccuracy found by such test. If any meter shall fail to register for any period,
Member and Deseret shall cooperate in good faith to estimate the amount of energy furnished during
such period.

                                                    7. RIGHT OF ACCESS.                Duly authorized
representatives of either party hereto shall be permitted to enter the premises of the other party hereto
at all reasonable times in order to carry out the provisions hereof.

                                                 8. CONTINUITY OF SERVICE.                    Deseret
shall use reasonable diligence to provide a constant and uninterrupted supply of electric power and
energy hereunder. If the supply of electric power and energy shall fail or be interrupted, or become
defective through act of God or a public enemy, or because of accident, labor troubles, or any other
cause beyond the control of Deseret, Deseret shall not be liable therefor or for damages caused
 thereby.

                                                    9. REGULATORY               APPROVALS          AND
OTHER ACTIONS. This Agreement shall be subject to any necessary regulatory approvals. At
Deseret's request, Member will use its best efforts to obtain or assist in obtaining any approvals or
orders that may be necessary from any regulatory authority in connection with the approval,
implementation or enforcement of this Agreement. Member shall also take such further or additional
steps or actions as may reasonably be requested by Deseret to assist in implementing and operating
under this Agreement. Other than as specifically set forth herein: (i) Except with the written consent
of the other party, neither Deseret nor Member, nor any person or entity acting or purporting to act on
behalf or with the authority of either, may change or adjust the rates, term, or any other provision
contained in this Agreement; (ii) neither Deseret nor Member, nor any person or entity acting or
purporting to act on behalf or with the authority of either, may seek or request from, or support any
request to, any agency, authority, person or entity exercising or purporting to exercise any regulatory
or ratemaking rights or authority, for any change or adjustment to the rates, term, or any other
provision of this Agreement; and (iii) to the fullest extent permitted by law, no person, entity, agency
or authority exercising or purporting to exercise any regulatory or ratemaking rights or authority,
whether on its own motion or at the request of any person or entity, may change or adjust, or seek to
change or adjust, the rates, term, or any other provision contained in this Agreement, whether pursuant
to a "just and reasonable" standard of review or any other standard of review, except to the limited
extent such agency or authority may have an indefeasible statutory right to adjust the rates or other
provisions of this Agreement to the extent they are determined to be contrary to the public interest.

                                                 10. EFFECTIVE DATE. Upon execution by
both parties, this Agreement shall become effective and binding effective April 1, 1996, subject to any
necessary regulatory approvals.

                                                     11. STRANDED COSTS. Each party hereby
acknowledges that, in participating in the Workout and entering into agreements and documents in
connection therewith, each party is relying upon this Agreement and upon the other party's good faith
compliance with all of the terms, conditions and obligations set forth in this Agreement. The parties
acknowledge and agree that (i) Deseret and its creditors have incurred and will incur significant costs
in order to fulfill Deseret's obligations under this Agreement and predecessor agreements; (ii) Deseret
and its creditors will not suffer or incur any stranded costs vis-a-vis Member so long as Member
purchases power and energy from Deseret under this Agreement, and the current and future electric
consumers located within Member's current certificated service areas purchase power and energy
from Member, throughout the initial term of this Agreement (through December 31, 2025); (iii)
Deseret and its creditors will suffer or incur significant stranded costs if, as a result of federal or state
legislation, regulation or action, Member is permitted to terminate or modify its obligations to
purchase power and energy from Deseret under this Agreement, or any current or future electric
consumers located within Member's current certificated service areas are permitted to obtain power
and energy from a supplier other than Member, prior to the end of the initial term of this Agreement
(on December 31, 2025); (iv) Deseret, on behalf of itself and its creditors, may recover any and all
such stranded costs suffered or incurred to the full extent the same are determined to be recoverable
by an appropriate regulatory authority; and (v) while it is not possible in advance to specify with
particularity the stranded costs that may be suffered or incurred, such stranded costs will include at
 least the net present value of (A) any estimated revenue stream lost, (B) minus the estimated
competitive market value of the released or unused capacity and associated energy, (C) over the
remaining initial term of this Agreement (through December 31, 2025).

                                              12. NO ASSIGNMENT. No assignment by
Deseret or Member of this Agreement or any rights hereunder, other than an assignment for security
purposes in connection with borrowings by Deseret or Member, shall be valid without the written
consent of the other party.

                                                  13. MERGERS, SALES, TRANSFERS, ETC.
 Neither party may, without the prior written consent of the other party, merge or consolidate with or
into any other entity. Member hereby covenants and agrees that, without the prior written consent of
Deseret, no significant assets, customers or service territory of Member will be sold, leased or
transferred to any other person or entity, and no other person or entity will provide retail electric
services within Member's certificated service areas; provided, however, that the continued provision
of retail electric services within Member's certificated service areas by any person or entity that
provided such services as of the effective date of this Agreement shall not constitute a breach of this
covenant. In the event any such sale, lease, transfer or provision of service occurs over the objection
and without the consent or encouragement of Member as a result of the exercise by others of powers
or rights under state or federal laws, including, without limitation, laws relating to eminent domain,
annexation, municipalization or retail wheeling (a "Taking"), Member promises and agrees to use its

any available sources, any and all resulting damages, whether direct or indirect, including generation,
transmission and related costs and damages owed to Deseret for a Taking or for a breach of Member's
covenants under this paragraph ("Deseret Damages"). Deseret promises and agrees to waive and not
to collect from Member any Deseret Damages arising from a Taking (including stranded costs
referenced in paragraph 11, above, resulting from a Taking), to the extent such damages exceed the
net amounts recovered by Member from others in the exercise of its best reasonable efforts as required
herein. Nothing in this paragraph is intended to prevent Member from pledging all or a substantial
portion of its assets as security for loans.

                                                  14. AUDIT RIGHTS. Not more often than once
per calendar year, upon reasonable advance written notice and during normal business hours, either
party may, at its own expense, review, audit and copy the other party's books, records and data relating
to this Agreement or the other party's compliance with the same, and both parties agree to cooperate
reasonably and in good faith in connection with any such audit or review.

                                                 15. ENTIRE AGREEMENT. This Agreement,
together with the Schedules hereto, constitute the entire agreement between the parties with respect
to the subject matter hereof. This Agreement may not be modified or amended without the written
agreement of both parties.

                                                   16. NOTICE AND CURE. In the event of a
default hereunder, the defaulting party shall cure such default within 30 days (5 days in the event of a
default in the payment of amounts due) after receipt of written notice of such default.
                                                    17. TERM.         This Agreement shall become
effective as of April 1, 1996, and shall remain effective through an initial term ending on December
31, 2025. This Agreement shall remain effective after the initial term unless and until it is terminated
by either party by giving to the other party not less than six (6) months' advance written notice of its
intention to terminate.

               load(s), and thereafter to the extent such load(s) continue to form any material
               portion of a Large Industrial and Commercial Load as otherwise defined hereunder.
                 Any retail load(s) which, through growth, change in character or operation, or any
               combination thereof is reasonably anticipated to exceed the threshold size set forth
               herein shall be deemed and treated as a Large Industrial and Commercial Load
               beginning with the first day of the first calendar month in which the load (or
               aggregated load) is reasonably anticipated to exceed the threshold.
               Notwithstanding the foregoing, in no event shall any retail load which Deseret, in its
                reasonable judgments, deems to be primarily agricultural, governmental, or
               charitable in nature, be included in any aggregation or otherwise be deemed to
               constitute a Large Industrial and Commercial Load.



               c.      “Large Load Threshold” shall mean 2.5 MW peak demand, or such other
               quantity (in MW) greater than 2.5 MW that: (i) Deseret’s Board of Trustees shall
               approve from time to time during the term of this Renewal Agreement; and (ii) all
               creditors of Deseret under the ORA have approved in writing during the term of the
               ORA as the same may be modified or extended; and (iii) would not result in any
               default of any written covenant, agreement or instrument to which Deseret or its
               subsidiary is a party.

D.     Minimum Bill:

The monthly minimum bill will be the Facilities Charge and Meter Reading and Billing
Charge as described in Sections C.1 and C.2.

E.     Billing Demand:

Billing Demand in kilowatts is the individual Member's 60- minute demand contribution to the
Deseret system peak load. The Deseret system peak load is defined as the maximum monthly sum
of the coincident 60-minute Member demands including loads billed under rates set in contracts
for Large Industrial and Commercial Loads (“Negotiated Contract Rates”). For billing purposes,
the Member's 60-minute demand contribution shall exclude the demand of loads served under
Negotiated Contract Rates measured at the time of the Deseret system peak. Measurements shall
be made at Deseret's points of interconnection and Member's resource interconnections. In the
absence of adequate measurement, Billing Demand shall be based on the best estimate available
and shall be agreed to by the Member and Deseret.

F.     Billing Energy:

Billing Energy is all energy in kilowatt-hours delivered to Member from all resources, as adjusted for
loads served under Negotiated Contract Rates. Measurements shall be made at or adjusted to
Deseret's points of interconnection and Member's resource interconnections. In the absence of
adequate measurement, Billing Energy shall be based on the best estimate available and shall be
agreed to by the Member and Deseret.

G.      Negotiated Contracts; Large Industrial and Commercial Load:

Any Large Industrial and Commercial Load (as defined above) shall be served under a Negotiated
Contract Rates. The rates and terms of such contracts will be negotiated between Deseret and
 the Member on a case-by-case basis; rates, charges, and terms of such contracts may be
established pursuant to any market based ratemaking authority granted or recognized to Deseret.

In the absence of a Negotiated Contract Rate Agreement for service to a Large Industrial and
Commercial Load, Member shall receive all such wholesale service requirements for service to
such load(s) pursuant to the rates and terms in effect from time to time under the Deseret Rate
Schedule “C”, which rates and terms may be promulgated, adjusted, and established by the
Governing Board of Deseret pursuant to any market based ratemaking authority granted or
recognized to Deseret.

Deseret may make available Negotiated Contracts to enable a Member to serve at-risk loads that
Deseret determines to be economically beneficial that may be lost unless a Negotiated Contract
rate is made available. The rates and terms of such contracts will be negotiated between Deseret
and the Member on a case-by-case basis.

H.     Power Factor:

The rates above are based on the Member maintaining at all times a power factor of 90% (lagging) or
higher as determined by measurement. Should the power factor, as metered at the points of
interconnection, not be maintained within such limits, Deseret shall notify the Member and request
that the power factor be corrected. If the Member has not begun corrective action at the end of 90
days, corrective action may be taken and the Member shall be obligated to compensate Deseret for
all sums expended.

I.     Excess Facilities Charge:

Whenever a Member's wholesale power contract with Deseret provides for supply of electricity in a
manner which will require service at a voltage level below 138 kV, such facilities will be provided
pursuant to a monthly excess Facilities Charge based on the cost to Deseret for such facilities.
Whenever a Member’s wholesale power contract with Deseret provides for delivery of electricity
(power or energy) at a New POD (as set forth in Section 6.a), an additional excess Facilities Charge
will apply based on and equal to the additional cost(s) incurred by Deseret to make deliveries to
such point(s), which additional costs: (i) shall in no event be less than zero ($0); and (ii) shall be
sufficient to cover all payments made and costs incurred by Deseret for services related to
deliveries on, over, or through facilities or provider(s) other than a provider making delivery of such
power and energy to an existing Deseret POD.

J.     Payment Terms:

         1.      When Bills are Payable
 On or before the twentieth (20th) day of each month, Deseret shall render to each Member a
monthly billing statement for charges for services furnished during the previous month determined
in accordance with this Rate Schedule. All bills are due and payable no later than the fifth day after
the end of the month in which the invoice was prepared.

If all or a portion of a monthly billing statement is disputed, payment shall be made in full. Deseret
shall reimburse any amount determined to have been correctly disputed, with a simple interest
charge thereon equal to one percent (1%) per month on the reimbursed amount, pro-rated by days,
until such amount owed, including interest, is paid in full.

        2. Late Payment Charge

A monthly late payment charge will be added by Deseret when payments are not received within
five (5) days after the end of the month in which the invoice is mailed to the Member. In the event
the Bills are not rendered by the twentieth (20th) day of the month the final due date shall be fifteen
(15) days after the date on which the bill is issued. If the scheduled payment date falls on other than
a business day, the payment is due on the next normal business day. The late payment charge for
each day beyond the final due date shall be computed as the simple interest on the unpaid balance
at a rate of 1 percent per month, pro-rated by days. The late payment charge will be added to the
billing amount for the next month. Payments will be credited against the most delinquent charges.

K.     General Terms and Conditions:

        1. Service under this Schedule will be in accordance with the terms of the Renewal
Wholesale Power Contract between the Member and Deseret and any electric service regulations
of Deseret on file with and approved by the Rural Utilities Services (RUS), any other regulatory
authority having proper jurisdiction, or (if no other regulatory authority applies) the governing board
of Deseret.

        2. The rates specified in this Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule “A” may be revised
periodically by Deseret's Board of Trustees to reflect: (a) changes in Deseret's production costs
(exclusive of debt service costs); (b) changes in Deseret’s debt service requirements beginning
January 1, 2026; (c) and, beginning January 1, 2026, other changes in costs incurred by Deseret.

The rates specified in this Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule “A” shall be revised periodically by
Deseret's Board of Trustees to reflect changes in costs of Member Resources. Member Resource
costs will be based upon budget projections as approved by Deseret's Board of Trustees. Any rate
changes will be subject to approval by any regulatory authority having proper jurisdiction.
