       This Agreement (the “‘Agreement") is dated as of June 1, 2025, among DESERET
GENERATION & TRANSMISSION CO-OPERATIVE, a Utah non-profit corporation
("Deseret"); BRIDGER VALLEY ELECTRIC ASSOCIATION, INC. ("Bridger Valley");
DIXIE-ESCALANTE ELECTRIC ASSOCIATION, INC. ("Dixie"); GARKANE ENERGY
COOPERATIVE, INC. ("Garkane"); MOON LAKE ELECTRIC ASSOCIATION, INC.
("Moon Lake"); and MT. WHEELER POWER, INC. ("Mt. Wheeler") (Bridger Valley, Dixie,
Garkane, Moon Lake, and Mt. Wheeler are hereinafter referred to collectively as the
"Members" and each one a "Member").

                                      RECITALS

   A. Deseret and the Members are a party to a Certain Member Rate "A" Discretionary
      Rate Rebate Agreement dated as of February 26, 2003 (the "Discretionary Rate
      Rebate Agreement")

   B. Deseret is party to certain agreements, some of which are listed below:

         i.   The Conformed, Amended & Restated Obligations Restructuring
              Agreement effective as of January 1, 2018, among Deseret, Blue Mountain
              Energy, Inc. ("BME"), National Rural Cooperative Finance Corporation
              ("CFC"), and National Cooperative Service Corporation ("NCSC"), as the
              same has been amended (the "CORA");

        ii.   .     Certain Wholesale Power Contracts (the "Member Contracts") between
              Deseret and each of the Members, as the same has been amended; and

       iii.    Certain Resource Integration Agreements (the "Integration Agreements")
       between
            Deseret and each of the Members, respectively.

   C. Pursuant to the terms of the Discretionary Rate Rebate Agreement, the Member
       Contracts, and the Integration Agreements, Deseret is permitted, from time to time as its
        Board of Trustees may direct, to make use of certain accumulated cash flows in excess
       of required debt service payments (the "Retained Share") to, among other things, make
       rebates to Members (the "Member Rebates") designed to permit individual Members to
       respond to certain market developments, and/or otherwise to serve such purposes as
       Deseret's Board of Trustees may from time to time determine to be in the best interest
       of Deseret and/or its Members, collectively.

D. Deseret's Board of Trustees has developed and adopted a revised facilities charge under
   the wholesale Rate Schedule "A" for each member effective on or after January 1, 2027,
   and has approved a revision to the methodology to be applied in determining whether, and
   in what amounts, Member Rebates are to be made from the Retained Share and how such
   rebates are to be allocated among the Members (the "Adjusted Annual Facilities Charge
   and Rebated Methodology").

E. Deseret's Board of Trustees has unanimously recommended superseding and replacing
   the Discretionary Rate Rebate Agreement by adopting this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, for good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of
which are hereby acknowledged, the parties to this Agreement agree as follows:

1. Defined Terms. Unless otherwise defined herein, all capitalized terms used in this
   Agreement shall have the meanings assigned thereto in the CORA. In addition, the
   meaning set forth in the recitals to this Agreement, each of the following terms shall have
   the further meaning indicated below:
2.
       a. The term Rebate as used herein shall mean and refer to any adjustment to the
           rates actually charged and collected by Deseret from its Members, either pursuant
           to Rate Schedule "A", Rate Schedule "B", any special or incentive contracts, or
           otherwise, which adjustment: (i) has the effect of decreasing the actual amount paid
           by any Member for electric power and/or service received from Deseret; (ii) is
           determined, in amount and timing, by Deseret's Board of Trustees from time to time
           after consideration of Deseret's available unrestricted cash position, and is not part
           of a general redesign of any existing rate schedule or tariff; (iii) is not required
           pursuant to any term of any existing agreement between Deseret and one or more of
           Deseret's creditors; and (iv) is not directly related to Deseret's cost(s) of production
           or to the costs for an integrated resource under the Resource Integration Agreement
           dated as of October 16, 1996 (as amended). Notwithstanding the foregoing, to the
           extent any adjustment in any rate, tariff, or contract arises or relates to any special
           circumstance pertaining to any individual member, any individual incentive load
           customer, or is otherwise intended to address a discreet and identifiable fact or
            circumstance pertaining to any one or more member(s) generally, such adjustment
           shall not be subject to nor governed by the provisions of this Agreement.

       b. The Adjusted Annual Facilities Charge and Rebate Methodology shall mean
           the policy set forth in the attached Schedule I.

3. Consent to Adjusted Annual Facilities Charge and Rebate Methodology. Subject to
   all the conditions to the Effective Date set forth in Paragraph 6 below, and during the
   term of this Agreement:

       a. Provided and for so long as Deseret shall consistently apply the Adjusted Annual
           Facilities Charge and Rebate Methodology, each of the Members hereby consent
          to Deseret's adoption, implementation, and use of the Adjusted Annual Facilities
          Charge Rebated Methodology.

       b. During the term of this Agreement, and subject to the terms of this Agreement,

          related to changes in Deseret's costs and contemplated by the Member Contracts

I, Brandon Worthington, state as follows:

                      I. INTRODUCTION AND QUALIFICATIONS

       1.     My name is Brandon Worthington. My business address is 10714 South Jordan
Gateway, Suite 300, South Jordan, Utah 84095. I am appearing on behalf of Deseret Generation
& Transmission Co-operative, Inc. d/b/a Deseret Power (“Deseret”). I am employed as Vice
President and Chief Financial Officer of Deseret.

       2.     I graduated from Utah Valley University in 2013 with a Bachelor of Science degree
in Accounting. I am a registered Certified Public Accountant licensed by the State of Utah.
Additionally, I graduated from the University of Utah with a Master of Accounting in 2016. I am
a member of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants, a professional organization.
                                                                             Exhibit No. DGT-0001
                                                                                      Page 2 of 14

       3.      I have been employed by Deseret since 2014. My prior positions at Deseret include
Financial Analyst from 2014 to 2017, Manager of Financial Reporting from 2017 to 2020,
Treasury Manager from 2020 to 2024, and Director of Member Rates and Relations from 2024
until October 2026, when I was promoted to Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. Prior to
working at Deseret, I was the Controller from 2012 to 2014 at Biomerics, LLC.

       4.      As Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, my responsibilities include ensuring
that Deseret’s accounting and financial reporting are maintained in accordance with generally
accepted accounting principles; developing and implementing Deseret’s fiscal policies and
procedures, financial controls, annual budgets, and accounting and auditing procedures; analyzing
Deseret’s financial results and developing strategic recommendations; overseeing treasury
management, including cash management, liquidity, investments, and short- and long-term cash
budgeting and forecasting; overseeing tax compliance and reporting and Deseret’s insurance
program; and ensuring compliance with Deseret’s debt covenants and maintaining its reporting to
and relationships with its creditors. I lead Deseret’s Accounting Department; Financial Reporting
and Insurance Department; Tax and Treasury Department; and Procurement Department. I also
report monthly to Deseret’s Board of Trustees on the financial position of Deseret and of its wholly
owned subsidiary, Blue Mountain Energy (“BME”). As Director of Member Rates and Relations
from 2024 to 2026, I was responsible for ensuring that Deseret’s wholesale power costs were
priced fairly and defensibly and for administering Deseret’s wholesale power supply contracts with
the Members, including contract negotiations, compliance monitoring and rate filings.

       5.      As Manager of Financial Reporting, I filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory
Commission (the “Commission”), on behalf of Deseret, FERC Form No. 1, Annual Report of
Major Electric Utilities, Licensees, and Others (“FERC Form 1”), and FERC Form No. 3-Q,
Quarterly Financial Report of Electric Utilities, Licensees, and Natural Gas Companies. I have
also prepared or assisted in preparing rate filings that Deseret submitted to the Commission for its
cost-based rates applicable to its Members, namely its 2023 filing in Docket No. ER24-105-000,
which was accepted for filing by the Commission on December 20, 2023. I am familiar with the
Commission’s Uniform System of Accounts and with the cost-allocation methods used in
preparing cost-based wholesale rates.
                                                                                 Exhibit No. DGT-0001
                                                                                          Page 3 of 14

                                   II. PURPOSE AND SUMMARY

        6.       This affidavit supports Deseret’s proposed increase in the rates of Renewal
Wholesale Rate Schedule A and Rate Schedule B in each Member’s Wholesale Power Contract,
designated as Rate Schedule FERC Nos. 100, 101, 103, 104 and 105. As discussed in greater
detail below and in the transmittal letter accompanying this filing, Deseret proposes to terminate
Rate Schedule FERC No. 102 after the culmination of this proceeding. The Members are the
distribution cooperatives described in Part III. I sponsor the Period I cost-of-service statements in
this filing, Statements AA through BM, which were prepared by me or under my direction and
supervision. Each of the Members consents to the rate change, and a copy of each such consent is
provided as Exhibit No. DGT-0002. My workpapers are provided as Exhibit No. DGT-0003.

changes to Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule A, effective January 1, 2027:

The meter charge and the annual facilities charges are not changed for either Renewal Wholesale
Rate Schedule A or Rate Schedule B.

        8.         As shown in Statement BK, the proposed rates would produce additional annual
revenue of approximately $4.0 million based on billing determinants for calendar year 2025, the
Period I test year (¶ 10), as shown in Part VI, ¶ 24. Because no Member takes service under Rate
Schedule B, the Rate Schedule B changes produce no additional revenue.

        9.         Each of the Members has consented to the proposed changes to Renewal Wholesale
Rate Schedule A and Rate Schedule B. The Members’ consent letters are included as Exhibit No.
DGT-0002. Because all wholesale customers in the affected rate class have consented, Deseret is
filing Period I statements only, as 18 C.F.R. § 35.13(d)(2)(ii)(B) permits.

        10.        Period I is calendar year 2025, the most recent calendar year for which audited
actual data are available. It ends no more than fifteen months before the date of this filing, as 18
C.F.R. § 35.13(d)(3)(i) requires. The rate design information required by 18 C.F.R. § 35.13(h)(37)
                                                                                Exhibit No. DGT-0001
                                                                                         Page 5 of 14

is provided in Statement BL. Statements AA through BM are based on Deseret’s 2025 FERC Form
1.

                   III. DESERET, ITS RESOURCES AND ITS MEMBERS

       11.       Deseret is a not-for-profit generation and transmission cooperative, formed by its
Member distribution cooperatives in the late 1970s. Its Members are:

             •   Bridger Valley Electric Association (“Bridger Valley”);

             •   Dixie Escalante Rural Electric Association, Inc. (“Dixie”);

             •   Garkane Energy Cooperative (“Garkane”);

             •   Moon Lake Electric Association (“Moon Lake”); and

             •   Mt. Wheeler Power (“Mt. Wheeler”)

(collectively, the “Members”).

Dixie also holds the Wholesale Power Contract of Flowell Electric Association, Inc. (“Flowell”),
which it acquired on January 1, 2021 and which is currently designated as Rate Schedule FERC
No. 102. Deseret provides requirements power supply and related services to the Members in Utah,
Nevada, Wyoming, Colorado and Arizona. In Period I, Deseret’s system coincident peak load was
555 MW, which includes 387 MW of Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule A load.

       12.       Deseret’s principal generating resources are:

             •   a 96.25% ownership interest in Bonanza Unit 1, a 458 MW (net) coal-fired unit in
                 Uintah County, Utah; and

             •   a 25.108% ownership interest in Hunter Unit 2, a 446 MW (net) coal-fired unit
                 operated by PacifiCorp in Emery County, Utah.

Both units are in PacifiCorp’s eastern balancing authority area. BME owns and operates the
Deserado mine, which is the sole long-term coal supplier to Bonanza Unit 1.

Deseret also wholly owns the following resources:
                                                                                 Exhibit No. DGT-0001
                                                                                          Page 6 of 14

             •   a peaking resource consisting of six natural gas-fired reciprocating engines with a
                 total nameplate capacity of 15 MW, known as the Solomon Generating Station,
                 located in St. George, Utah, placed in service in July 2022;

             •   a 12.5 MW AC (15 MW DC) photovoltaic generating facility located on land
                 adjacent to Bonanza Unit 1, placed in service in May 2023; and

             •   a peaking resource consisting of twenty-two natural gas-fired reciprocating
                 engines with a total nameplate capacity of approximately 50.5 MW adjacent to
                 Bonanza Unit 1, construction of which began in 2024, with completion expected
                 in mid-2027.

The Solomon Generating Station and Bonanza photovoltaic resources were in service throughout
Period I. The 50.5 MW resource was under construction during Period I, and none of its costs is
reflected in Period I operating expenses; the $862,691 of interest incurred on the project in 2025
was capitalized. Deseret expects debt service on that resource of approximately $8.4 million in
2027 and approximately $10.3 million per year beginning in 2028.

       13.       The Members also hold long-term purchase arrangements that are integrated with
Deseret’s resources under the Resource Integration Agreements, which are separately on file with
the Commission. These are described as Member Exempt Resources and delineated in exhibits to
each Member’s Renewal Wholesale Power Contract. Member Exempt Resources include:

             •   Member entitlements to an allocation of the Salt Lake City Area Integrated
                 Projects, marketed by the Western Area Power Administration, which the
                 Members have assigned to Deseret; and

             •   small run-of-river hydroelectric and portable diesel resources within Member
                 service areas, whose combined output at Deseret’s coincident peak hours reached
                 a maximum of 6.3 MW in Period I.

Deseret reimburses the Members for these resources and records the payments in purchased power
expense, FERC Account 555.

       14.       The Members and Flowell, whose Wholesale Power Contract was acquired by
Dixie in 2021 (¶ 11), also hold entitlements in the Intermountain Power Project (“IPP”) under
                                                                             Exhibit No. DGT-0001
                                                                                      Page 7 of 14

power sales contracts with the Intermountain Power Agency (“IPA”) that run through June 15,
2027. References to the Members of Deseret in this paragraph include Flowell. The entitlements
total 7.017% of the output of IPP’s two coal-fired units (900 MW net each): Moon Lake, 2.000%;
Mt. Wheeler, 1.786%; Dixie, 1.534%; Garkane, 1.267%; Bridger Valley, 0.230%; and Flowell,
0.200%. Under an Excess Power Sales Agreement dated December 1, 1980, the Members’ IPP
capacity and energy are sold to the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power and the cities of
Burbank, Glendale and Pasadena, California, unless and until the Members recall them. The
Members have not recalled their IPP entitlements in recent years, and no IPP costs are reflected in
Period I. In 2025, IPA replaced the coal-fired units with an 840 MW (net) natural gas-fired
combined-cycle plant (“IPP Renewed”): Unit 3 entered service on October 10, 2025, Unit 4
entered service on December 9, 2025, and the coal-fired units last generated on November 26,
2025. Under section 44.3 of the power sales contracts, IPP Renewed became the Project’s
generating station, and the Members’ existing entitlement percentages apply to its output through
June 15, 2027. Beginning June 16, 2027, the Members will take service under renewal power sales
contracts with IPA, with a combined entitlement of 7.082% of IPP Renewed (about 59 MW).
Because the Members’ IPP entitlements are sold rather than recalled, the transition from the coal-
fired units to IPP Renewed does not affect the Period I costs on which the proposed rates are based,
and Deseret does not expect it to affect the cost of serving Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule A
load in 2027.

       15.      Service under Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule A uses a four-part rate: (i) a meter
charge of $300.00 per month per point of delivery; (ii) a fixed annual facilities charge, apportioned
monthly and unique to each Member; (iii) Tier 1 and Tier 2 coincident demand rates; and (iv) Tier
1 and Tier 2 energy rates. Since January 1, 2024, the rate has also included seasonal demand and
energy surcharges (the “Seasonal Surcharges”). Tier 2 rates apply only to monthly demand and
energy above a threshold established for each Member in 2011 at its maximum use over the five-
year period 2003 through 2007, plus 10%. Those thresholds have not changed since 2011. Service
to Member retail loads above 2.5 aggregated MW of peak demand (“Large Load”) is provided
under separate agreements between Deseret and the Member serving that load, which the Renewal
Wholesale Power Contracts call “Large Customer Agreements” (section 2(b)(iv) of each Renewal
Wholesale Power Contract). Under the Renewal Wholesale Power Contracts, the rates and terms
                                                                               Exhibit No. DGT-0001
                                                                                        Page 8 of 14

of each Large Customer Agreement are negotiated case by case and are transacted pursuant to
Deseret’s market-based rate tariff. By mutual agreement, a Large Customer Agreement may
provide the benefit of Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule A rates for the initial 2.5 MW of the
Large Load, or a greater amount if the 2.5 MW threshold is adjusted after the initial term of the
contract. As of the date of this affidavit, there are ten Large Customer Agreements. This filing
does not change the rates under any Large Customer Agreement.

       16.     Because Deseret is a cooperative, margins it earns are returned to the Members.
The return can be applied as rebates or as patronage capital. In Period I, Deseret provided Member
rebates totaling $6.46 million under the rebate provisions of Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule A
(Exhibits C-4 and C-5). In 2025, Deseret filed and the Commission accepted a change to those
provisions in Docket No. ER26-17-000. In addition to increasing the annual facilities charge to
an aggregate total of $7.5 million (from $6.628 million), the change provided that, if Deseret has
sufficient unrestricted cash reserves (accumulated cash flows in excess of required debt service
payments, or “Retained Shares”), it will provide a rebate of the full $7,500,000 of annual facilities
charges to all Members in any given future year. Further, the new provisions explain that if Deseret
cannot make the full Rate Rebate on account of Retained Shares in a calendar year, Deseret will
place limits on its rotation of allocated capital to any of its Members during the year, continuing
until a subsequent Rate Rebate is paid to Members. “Rotation of allocated” capital refers to the
cooperative’s periodic retirement and refunding of previously allocated patronage capital to its
Members, generally on a first-in, first-out basis. The new negotiated provisions among Deseret
and its Members also contain certain terminations of historic discretionary rate rebates, mutual
releases of claims to future rate rebates, past and future allocations and/or rotations of net adjusted
margins or patronage capital, and covenants not to pursue released claims. Deseret expects
Member rebates in 2027 to total $7.5 million, as those provisions permit. This filing does not
change the rebate provisions.



                                 IV. FINANCIAL STRUCTURE

       17.     Deseret became subject to the Commission’s jurisdiction on October 16, 1996,
when a restructuring of its obligations transferred its Rural Utilities Service debt to the National
                                                                           Exhibit No. DGT-0001
                                                                                    Page 9 of 14

Rural Utilities Cooperative Finance Corporation (“CFC”). That restructuring, the 1998 acquisition
of the Bonanza Unit 1 interest, and later amendments were consolidated in a Conformed
Obligations Restructuring Agreement with CFC, effective January 1, 2018 (the “2018 CORA”).
Under the 2018 CORA, CFC’s forbearance on Deseret’s original mortgage debt was conditioned
on Deseret making scheduled Minimum Payments through December 31, 2025, including
$61,450,000 in each of 2024 and 2025.

        18.     Deseret satisfied all of the Minimum Payments required under the 2018 CORA
through December 31, 2025. At December 31, 2025, Deseret’s remaining obligations under the
2018 CORA were a $9.6 million note due in 2026 and a final Available Extra Cash Flow payment
of approximately $2.9 million. The $2.9 million was paid in March of 2026 and the $9.6 million
is to be paid quarterly throughout 2026, with the final quarterly payment in December of 2026.
The original notes were cancelled as of March 31, 2026. The $9.6 million note is a separate note
under the 2018 CORA and, after the March 2026 payment, is Deseret’s only remaining obligation
under it.

        19.     All of Deseret’s long-term debt is owed to CFC. At December 31, 2025, Deseret’s
notes payable to CFC totaled $117.5 million, of which $13.1 million was current and $104.4
million long-term, consisting of: $39.4 million outstanding under a $156.2 million credit
agreement maturing September 30, 2043; $36.0 million outstanding under a $112.0 million facility
maturing December 31, 2049; two notes maturing September 30, 2047, with $19.2 million and
$13.2 million outstanding; and the $9.6 million note due in 2026 described in ¶ 18. The term notes
amortize quarterly, and the two larger facilities were only partly drawn at December 31, 2025. In
2025, Deseret borrowed $71 million of new debt, mostly under the two larger facilities, to fund
capital spending on the Bonanza Unit 1 selective catalytic reduction (“SCR”) project and the 50.5
MW peaking resource described in ¶ 12. Excluding the $9.6 million note, Deseret’s debt at
December 31, 2025 was approximately $107.9 million of conventional amortizing debt, with
scheduled maturities of approximately $3.5 million in 2026, $3.6 million to $4.0 million per year
from 2027 through 2030 and $89.2 million thereafter. Further information appears in the Notes to
Financial Statements in Deseret’s 2025 FERC Form 1 at pages 122-123, included in Period I,
Statement AA.
                                                                                     Exhibit No. DGT-0001
                                                                                             Page 10 of 14

                              V. EXPLANATION OF THE RATE CHANGE

        20.        Cost drivers. Deseret’s costs of serving Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule A load
have increased since rates were last set in 2022 and 2024. Using a compound annualized five-year
lookback comparison, the principal drivers are:

                                                               Compound annual
                                                                                       Share of 2025
 Cost category                      2020     2025 (Period I)   growth rate, 2020–
                                                                                       operating expense
                                                               2025
 Fuel                              $80.5M        $92.0M               2.7%                    38.2%
 Purchased power                   $41.9M        $60.2M               7.5%                    25.0%
 Administrative and general        $17.7M        $19.9M               2.4%                     8.3%


Fuel expense, Deseret’s largest cost, rose from $80.5 million in 2020 to $92.0 million in 2025, a
compound annual growth rate of 2.7%, and represented 38.2% of Deseret’s 2025 operating
expenses. Purchased power expense rose from $41.9 million to $60.2 million, or 7.5% per year,
and represented 25.0% of 2025 operating expenses. Administrative and general expense rose from
$17.7 million to $19.9 million, or 2.4% per year. Deseret attributes these increases principally to
general inflation. These increases are reflected in the Period I data.

        21.        Period I results. As shown in Statement BK, Deseret’s Period I net loss was
$8,993,809. With or without the proposed increase, revenues from Member load served under
Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule A yield no net income.

        22.        Board approval. The Deseret Board of Trustees approved the proposed changes
to Renewal Wholesale Rate Schedule A on August 20, 2026, and to Rate Schedule B on October
22, 2026, and authorized Deseret’s management to file them with the Commission. The purpose
of the increase is to address increased expenses, decreased margins on sales to non-Members, and
coverage of Deseret’s debt service obligations. Between 2020 and 2025 (Period I), Deseret’s non-
Member revenue declined at a compound annual rate of 5.8%.

        23.        Uniform increase across Tier 1, Tier 2 and the Seasonal Surcharges. Unlike the
2022 rate change, which left Tier 2 unchanged, Deseret proposes to raise every volumetric
component by approximately 5%. Tier 2 was adopted in 2011 to give Members a cost-causation
signal against load growth above historical levels: to promote demand-side efficiency and to defer
                                                                               Exhibit No. DGT-0001
                                                                                       Page 11 of 14

higher-cost resource acquisitions. The Seasonal Surcharges were adopted in 2024 (i) to address
growth in the Members’ system demand and the need to acquire sufficient resources to meet
seasonal periods of high demand, and (ii) as in Deseret’s prior rate cases accepted by the
Commission, to use rate design to send pricing signals that encourage energy efficiency and
conservation during peak seasonal periods. If Tier 1 rose and the Tier 2 adders and Seasonal
Surcharges stayed fixed, those adders would shrink relative to the base rate and the signals would
weaken. A uniform percentage increase keeps the existing relationship among the components. It
also spreads the revenue requirement in proportion to how each Member uses the system, including
during peak seasons.
